card.title: Nintendo Switch Common Power, Charging, and Video Output Faults

claims.statement: A blank screen or freezing issue on version 7.x.x firmware can sometimes be temporarily mitigated by leaving the console charging overnight and holding it in recovery mode, or placing it in RCM mode to inject the hekate payload.
claims.evidence: If the screen turns right on with hekate payload, your console is fine, the firmware is not.
claims.quote: If you know that your console is in version 7.x.x, sorry but for now the only thing that you can do is leave it charging all night and trying to put it to recovery mode...

claims.statement: If the payload method fails completely, the PI3USB30532 chip may be bad or the CPU is dead.
claims.evidence: If even the payload method failed, you probably will have a PI3USB30532 bad or the CPU is just dead af.
claims.quote: If even the payload method failed, you probably will have a PI3USB30532 bad or the CPU is just dead af.

claims.statement: For HDMI docking issues with no image output, check that 3V is reaching the PI3USB30532 chip and inspect the surrounding passives, ferrite filters, and caps.
claims.evidence: Check around the passives around PI3USB. In particular the ferrite filters.
claims.quote: If no image on HDMI docking - Check 3v is getting to the PI3USB. Now this is important... Does the dock LED go green and the TV attempts to find a signal?

claims.statement: A bricked console is frequently a console with a faulty charge controller IC on the motherboard preventing it from charging even when the port is intact.
claims.evidence: If this ic goes bad then the console will not charge even when the charge port is good.
claims.quote: Many times a 'bricked' console is actually just a console that has a faulty charge controller on the motherboard.

claims.statement: Resistor values like 3.8k and 5.6k on the bq24193 charging circuit are critical for setting battery temperature ranges; substituting incorrect values will prevent battery charging.
claims.evidence: If you replace the 5.6kohm resistor with 10k ,bq 24193 will not charge the battery because the temp set for charghing will bee out of range.
claims.quote: For example if you replace the 5.6kohm resistor with 10k ,bq 24193 will not charge the battery...

procedure: {'step': 'Unscrew and remove the back case of the Nintendo Switch.'}
{'step': 'Remove the motherboard from the console housing.'}
{'step': 'Apply soldering flux to all connection points of the broken charging port.'}
{'step': 'Carefully heat the charging port connection points using a hot air soldering tool until the port can be gently lifted off, avoiding motherboard bubbling from overheating.'}
{'step': 'Slowly heat the solder on the board pads and attach the new charging port.'}
{'step': 'Reinstall the motherboard into the console and reattach the back cover.'}
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Using third-party docks or incorrect USB-C cables can result in permanent console damage, slow charging, or bricking.
card.caveats: Diagnostic steps mix general troubleshooting guidance with component-level identification notes; verify board revisions before performing reflow or replacement.
